title: Audit-driven quota corrections and safe rollback procedure for billing reconciliations
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Problem statement: We have observed edge cases where quota window resets and late usage backfills cause billing mismatches for tenants on reserved capacity. Root causes include out-of-order usage events, clock skew across regions, and ad-hoc correction scripts without an explicit audit trail. Goal: implement an audit-trail-driven quota correction flow with safe, idempotent rollback so billing adjustments and quota state changes are traceable, reversible, and can be replayed deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: All quota corrections emit an immutable audit event (correction_event) stored in the ledger with origin, reason, and causal_version
Automated correction jobs are idempotent and include an idempotency key tied to invoice_id or correction_batch_id
Backfilled usage that affects invoices triggers a draft invoice flag and a reviewable credit proposal (no silent invoice mutations)
Reserved capacity pools reconcile without double-dipping: correction must decrement pool allocation only once and create a compensation_event if previously over-allocated
A rollback API exists to revert a correction_event within the allowed SLA window and creates a compensating event recorded in the audit ledger
Unit and integration tests cover out-of-order event application, region failover, and time-skew scenarios
Dashboards display correction_event rates, affected customers, and pending draft invoices
implementation_notes: Model: introduce correction_event table in usage ledger with fields: event_id, tenant_id, causality_token, base_events[], net_token_delta, reason_enum, created_by, created_at, applied_at, rollback_of_event_id
Engine: correction runner uses causal_version to determine idempotent application order. Use per-tenant sequence numbers to guarantee deterministic ordering during replay
APIs: expose POST /internal/quotas/corrections to create a correction_event and GET /internal/quotas/corrections/{id} to inspect. Public-facing billing portal surfaces correction proposals

Reserved pools: add a two-phase commit for pool decrements. Phase 1: reserve compensation slot; Phase 2: apply decrement and emit compensation_event. If failure, release reservation and mark correction_event FAILED
Backfill: write a dry-run mode for backfill to compute delta and generate draft invoices. Run small batches (<100 tenants) initially to validate economics
Edge cases: handle clock skew by using ledger logical time (monotonic counter) instead of wallclock for ordering. Translate wallclock to tenant timezone only for presentation layer
Security: correction API requires billing-admin and ops role; calls must be logged with requestor and rationale
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): deploy correction_event schema and runner in staging. Run synthetic backfills to ensure idempotency
Phase B (limited): enable for internal billing team on 10 pilot tenants (no auto invoice mutation, show draft credits only)
Phase C (gradual): enable auto-apply for low-risk corrections (<0.5% of monthly usage) with human review for larger deltas
Phase D (full): open to all tenants and integrate with invoice generation once monitoring thresholds are green for 7 days

2025-02-01: Integration testing: created small backfill affecting reserved pools. Discovered double-apply when previous partial failure left reservation locked. Mitigation: two-phase commit and compensation_event. - Samantha
